messages:
customer-success-jane: FYI customer ACME (tenant acme-123) just escalated — their latency dashboard tenant view lost p95/p99 lines after the eu1 regional cutover at ~08:12 UTC. org-level view still shows overall series but tenant-level percentiles are blank. ticket#7892. customer is worried.

mia_support: ack — thanks for flagging. can you paste the exact dashboard + panel link and any repro steps the customer used? also asked them to confirm tenant id (acme-123) — got it.

ashwin_sre: which panel type? timeseries quantile panel or a custom query? quick triage: are raw histograms / quantile series present in the metrics backend or is it just the frontend rendering?

customer-success-jane: panel: "Latency / p95 p99 (tenant)" under Observability -> SLOs -> acme-123. Customer clicked tenant view and chart lines for p95/p99 are gone, only p50 shows. They said trying org view shows p95/p99 there. No changes on their side.

deploy-bot: region-eu1-cutover r-20260305-eu1 completed at 2026-03-05T08:12:07Z :white_check_mark: (canary 100%)

elaine_prod: digging into the ingest transform logs now. early finding: during the cutover we toggled a telemetry flag that runs label flattening. It appears the transform renamed the percentile series label from `tenant_id` -> `top_level_org` for some child-tenant series, which the tenant-level dashboard queries are filtering on. org-level queries still match because they use `top_level_org`.

ashwin_sre: can you paste an example query and raw output? show me the series labels for acme-123.

elaine_prod: running a quick query against metrics-store: 
```
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/query?expr=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_id))&tenant=acme-123' | jq .
```
result: `[]` (empty series). same query without tenant filter returns series with `top_level_org=acme` set.

mia_support: workaround while we fix: in the dashboard panel settings toggle to org view, or modify panel query to reference `top_level_org` instead of `tenant_id` for affected customers. pinging docs to add temporary note in ticket.

ashwin_sre: confirms this is likely the flag flip. action plan: revert flattening for eu1 ingest, or add compatibility mapping that preserves `tenant_id` label for legacy dashboards. will prioritize revert then roll a clean transform. assigning to @ashwin_sre, ETA ~1h for hotfix + verification.

customer-success-jane: conveyed to ACME — they prefer minimal changes so a revert is fine. they've accepted 1h window.

ashwin_sre: rolling hotfix now: reverting `flatten-org-labels` for ingest-eu1, staging patch, will bump canary.

deploy-bot: rollout r-20260305-eu1-revert started (canary) :arrow_forward:

ashwin_sre: hotfix applied to ingest-eu1 canary, waiting 3m for metrics to repopulate, will escalate to full rollout if good.

elaine_prod: I can confirm ingest logs now show original `tenant_id` labels emitted for requests from acme-123.

ashwin_sre: after revert, I queried the same endpoint: 
```
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/query?expr=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_id))&tenant=acme-123' | jq .
```
result: series present (p99 back). pushing full rollback to eu1.

mia_support: updated ticket#7892 with RCA and workaround + ETA. told ACME p95/p99 should reappear shortly.

customer-success-jane: ACME confirmed p95/p99 are back in their tenant dashboard. thanks team. :tada:

ashwin_sre: follow-up items: 1) add compatibility test to ingest transforms to ensure `tenant_id` preserved for tenant-level queries, 2) add canary guardrail to prevent label renames without a compatibility shim, 3) docs entry for ops runbook. will open PRs and link in ticket.

elaine_prod: opened internal PR #3124 for transform compatibility, assigned review to @ashwin_sre.

ashwin_sre: closing loop — full rollback to eu1 complete at 2026-03-05T08:44:12Z, monitoring dashboards for 30m. will update ticket after the window."
